create.name: Buddhist Library and Meditation Centre
create.bio:
Sydney's Buddhist Library is a charitable centre that belongs to no single school of Buddhism, and it has recently moved into new premises in Glebe. Run by the Buddha Dharma Education Fund, a registered charity, it keeps a lending collection of more than 7,000 books and recordings across all the main Buddhist schools, open to members of the public, and offers a quiet place in the city to read, meet and sit.

Its programme draws on teachers from many traditions rather than one lineage. Most events ask only for a donation: guided lunchtime meditation on Thursdays, Tuesday evening talks with meditation and discussion, Sunday mindfulness groups for people who have already done a course, Zen sitting, a monthly Buddhism discussion group and a book group, along with gentle yoga and qi yoga classes. Its team page lists resident and visiting teachers, from local insight and Zen teachers to monastics of the Theravada, Mahayana and Tibetan schools. Recordings of past talks and courses, among them a five-part series on early Buddhist theory of knowledge with Bhante Sujato, are on its YouTube channel.

free_resources.title: Thursday Lunchtime Meditation
free_resources.description: A short guided meditation in the middle of the working week, led in turn by teachers from different Buddhist traditions and open to beginners and experienced meditators. Offered by donation.

free_resources.title: Tuesday Evening Talks
free_resources.description: A weekly evening of teaching with a changing guest, which may include a Dhamma talk, guided meditation, questions and group discussion, offered by donation at the Glebe library.

free_resources.title: Sunday Mindfulness Meditation Group
free_resources.description: A monthly follow-up group led by Jim Teoh for people who have already completed an insight or mindfulness meditation course, with sitting and walking practice. Offered by donation.
